sources.title: Great Tits (Parus major) Reduce Caterpillar Damage in Commercial Apple Orchards
sources.locator: Abstract; Results; Materials and Methods, Experimental Design.
sources.scope: Primary field experiment in 12 commercial Dutch apple orchards (six integrated pest management, six organic) from 1997–2000; compared 2-hectare nest-box plots with breeding great tits against control plots.
sources.license: Creative Commons Attribution License, stated in the article copyright section; the article does not specify a numbered license version.
sources.rightsEvidenceLocator: Copyright statement after the article citation; Creative Commons Attribution License.
sources.attribution: Mols CMM, Visser ME (2007). Great Tits (Parus major) Reduce Caterpillar Damage in Commercial Apple Orchards. PLoS ONE 2(2):e202. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0000202. Claims are paraphrased.

claims.text: Across 12 Dutch commercial apple orchards studied from 1997–2000, caterpillar damage in integrated-pest-management plots with breeding great tits was 2.9%, compared with 5.8% in controls; the study did not demonstrate a similar reduction in organic orchards.
claims.scope: Twelve orchards, two management regimes, paired study plots, and the study period only.

gaps: No multi-source species dossier is added.
The study does not describe great-tit ecology outside the tested Dutch orchard settings.
